title: Continuity — launch film
logline: For design engineers who have seen too much sloppy AI video: Continuity gives agents a studio process and eyes, so what they make is good enough to ship. Open source.

scenes.intent: Name the problem in one breath: agents can write motion, but they can't see it.

beats.note: 'Agents can write motion.' rises word by word, in fg, a focus caret after it
line 1 steps back to the grey; 'They just can't see it.' rises (the scene's moment)
everything but 'see' steps back to the grey: the problem, picked out by ink

elements.note: First line of the scene's one statement: a single <Headline> (display, 112) holding l1 and l2 as block spans, left on the safe edge, vertically centred. fg, then the grey at b2.
A 6×96px caret in the focus colour after 'motion.': the agent typing. The only accent in the frame; blinks (m.blink) until b2.
Second line, directly under l1 (same Headline). fg; at b3 it steps back to the grey except 'see'.
Inline span inside l2, pinned to text-fg so it keeps its ink when the rest of l2 dims. Emphasis by ink, never a colour or italic.

scenes.motion: Solid canvas, no light (the world before eyes). b1: l1 maskUp by words (responsive, word stagger 40ms); the caret fades in with it and blinks until b2-0.08, then fades out. b2: l1 `dim` (instant) as l2 maskUp by words on the expressive spring — the scene's one moment. b3: l2 `dim` (instant); 'see' keeps fg. Camera 1 → 1.03 anchored on the safe left edge (origin x 96), so the type never drifts and the cut into the turn doesn't snap. Nothing exits; hard cut on the beat onto the field, and the cut lands on the turn's entrance: studio's label and headline start moving on its frame 0, so the eye goes from the held 'see' straight to the rising answer.

scenes.intent: The turn: Continuity gives agents a studio process, and eyes.

beats.note: label + headline start rising on the cut's first frame (the cut lands on an entrance), in fg, without 'eyes.'
'eyes.' lands on its own beat: the answer to the hook's 'see'
pipeline rail draws, the five stations rise along it
'Plan' takes focus: the process starts; its word steps out and the camera goes into the tile

scenes.motion: Stage bg `gradient` on `accent`: the first colour of the film, a moving cobalt field (the hero). b1 (frame 0, on the cut): label `fade`; headline maskUp by lines on the expressive spring (the moment), 'eyes.' held back. b2: `eyes` `fade` (responsive). b3: rail `draw` (slow, inOut); the five tags `rise` in reading order (list stagger 40ms) as it passes. b4: plan `ink` + plan-focus `fade` at the instant tier; the ring clears as the portal starts. The Plan tile is drawn at 16:9 (100 × 56) so the window keeps the tile's edge. Camera 1 → 1.03 anchored on the safe left edge, like the hook, and it lands when the portal starts (the portal is the scene's move). Out: a portal through the focused Plan tile — the field and the other stations fly past the camera, the tile fills the frame and opens onto chapter 01.

scenes.intent: Plan before pixels: the director writes a storyboard of scenes, copy and timed beats before any code.

beats.note: the portal lands: the storyboard window and '01 · Plan' were inside the tile; the headline masks up
rows, lanes and beat keyframes have landed
this scene's row takes the raised segment and steps up to fg

text.label: 01 · Plan
text.headline: Plan before pixels.
text.sub: Scenes and beats, timed before code.

elements.note: <Label> '01 · Plan' (repeats the station's word), 8px above the headline. On screen from frame 0: it is what the Plan tile opens onto.
<Headline> display (112), fg, in the 608px lockup column on the safe edge: ≤ 2 lines, broken by meaning. The product sits 96px to its right (litt's split frame).
<Body> (36, the grey), 32px under the headline.
<Window title="storyboard.json"> 1024×640 on the right (columns 7–12), vertically centred with the lockup. Body: `rows` left (448px), `lanes` right, a status bar at the bottom.

5 rows (rows-r0…r4, the List's 88px rhythm, 2px hairlines): 'hook · the problem' 3.6s | 'studio · the turn' 4.4s | 'plan · storyboard' 4.8s | 'check · eyes on frames' 7.0s | 'measure · motion chart' 5.0s. Titles in the grey; this scene's title (title2) steps up to fg.
The raised segment (surface-2, hairline + top highlight) behind this scene's row: P12's 'current item'.

scenes.motion: Solid canvas. In: the portal from studio's Plan tile — the scene opens from the tile's rounded rect, with '01 · Plan' and the storyboard window already on it (the bench is never empty); nothing else moves until the portal lands (0.9s). b1: headline maskUp lines on the expressive spring (the moment); sub `rise` as it lands. Lanes `wipeRight` from 1.2 (list 40ms), keyframes `fade` from 1.5 (40ms), all landed by b2. b3: `current` fades in and title2 `ink`s to fg. Camera 1 → 1.03 after the portal. Out: a layered carry, copy-led — the lockup stays and rides the cut: label, headline and sub lead the wave left (copy travels furthest), the board follows a beat later, so the frame peels off from the left edge into check.

scenes.intent: Eyes on every frame: the contact sheet shows a defect, the gate names it, the fix turns it green.

beats.note: the carry lands the sheet (frames on it) and the terminal in a wave, the sheet first; label slides in, headline masks up
`pnpm ct check launch` types as the terminal settles
RED: two findings tagged 'error', a danger ring on f5, the other frames recede, camera focus push; holds ≥ 1.4s
GREEN: f5's headline lifts off the CTA, the ring clears, 'error' → 'fixed', the ✔ line is placed, the sheet returns

text.headline: Eyes on every frame.
text.sub: A contact sheet and a gate, every cut.

scenes.motion: Solid canvas. In: plan's layered carry lands the sheet (its frames already on it) and the terminal still travelling left, the sheet first and the terminal a step behind (the wave), the label slides in the same way. b1: headline maskUp lines (responsive), sub rise. b2: the command types (24 cps) as the terminal settles; the scan line fades in. b3: report + findings `rise` (list); ring fades in at the instant tier; the other frames recede to 40% (slow, inOut); the camera focus-pushes 1.01 → 1.03 (slow, inOut). b4: f5b lifts 22px (responsive), f5c to full opacity, ring `fadeOut`; err → ok swap at the instant tier, titles `dim`; done-l0 `settle` — the scene's one moment; frames return. Out: product-led — the lockup leaves left first (an exit into the cut), then a layered carry takes the sheet and the gate left, the sheet leading, the terminal trailing, into measure.

scenes.intent: Motion, measured: rhythm, easing and dead air are numbers the agent checks, not vibes.

beats.note: the layered carry lands the lockup and the chart still travelling: the copy leads in from further right, the chart follows
the energy curve wipes on under the playhead, which is already running as the carry settles
three verdict tags are placed as the playhead lands
the lockup steps off left and the chart window slides left into the cut, accelerating: it becomes the score card

scenes.motion: Solid canvas. In: check's layered carry, copy-led on this side — label, headline and sub are on screen from the cut and ride in on the wave (copy travels furthest, leads), the chart window follows. b2: plot `wipeRight` and the playhead x tween share start, duration (linger) and ease (inOut). b3: the three tags `settle` in reading order (list 40ms) — the scene's one moment. Camera 1 → 1.03. b4 / Out: the lockup leaves left (exit), and the chart window slides left into the space it left, 236px on t² (accelerating, ≈ 31 px a frame on the last frame): the match hands that speed to critic's card.

scenes.intent: A critic scores every cut on five axes, and only the best version ships.

beats.note: the match lands: the score card has carried the chart window's speed across the frame and settled on the left; label slides in, headline masks up in the right column
meters fill and scores count
verdict: 'Ships', best of 3

<Stat value={4.6} decimals={1} label="v3 · mean score" unit="/ 5">, title size: label above value, tabular.
<Tag tone="success">Ships</Tag>, drawn at 16:9 (100 × 56) so the window keeps the tag's edge: the verdict as a word, and the portal's `via`: the camera goes through it into the end card.

<Caption> 'best of 3 versions', just before the tag.

scenes.motion: Solid canvas. In: a match from measure's chart window (match v2): the card starts where the window was, at the window's speed (≈ 940 px/s, left), and decelerates on one curve to the safe left edge, 468px along — the chart becomes the score card on its way across. The card makes no entrance of its own; its meters and counters wait for it to land. b1: label slides in, headline masks up, sub rises — in the right column the window left. b2: meter fills scaleX 0 → 1 and the five counters run together (slow, inOut, list 40ms); the mean counts over linger. b3: `ships` `settle` — the scene's one moment — and `best` fades in. `ships-word` steps out at the instant tier as the portal starts. ≈ 1.2s of settled hold before the portal. Camera 1 → 1.03, landing as the portal starts (the portal is the scene's move). Out: a portal through the 'Ships' tag — the card and the copy fly past the camera, the tag fills the frame and opens onto the end card, so the field's colour arrives through the verdict instead of on a full-frame cut.

scenes.motion: Stage bg `gradient` on `aurora` (colour returns for the brand; not `accent`, where the cobalt button would sink into the cobalt field). In: the portal through critic's 'Ships' tag — the card opens from the tag's rounded rect with the field and the button already on it; nothing else moves until it lands (0.8s). b2: wordmark `settle` (expressive) — the moment. b3: tagline `rise`. Then hold, settled, for more than 2s while the camera pushes 1 → 1.03 into the last frame, from the portal's landing. Last scene: the film ends on the held card.
